title: Market Pulse
body_html:
This post reflects my current views on the market, sectors, and internal breadth/momentum. Expect candid, data-driven analysis, peppered with personal insights drawn from years of trading experience. I aim to provide value in every edition, helping you to see the market through a clearer, more informed lens.

What You Can Expect

  • In-Depth Market Analysis: A thorough examination of market trends, key indices, and pivotal turning points.

  • Sector Spotlights: A closer look at the hottest (and not-so-hot) sectors, highlighting opportunities and risks.

  • Breadth and Momentum Insights: Understanding the underlying strength of the market through breadth indicators and momentum metrics.

  • Themes and Setups: A look at the top stocks in terms of relative strength, momentum, trend, volatility, and liquidity to spot themes, setups, and opportunities

Exclusive Features

  • Interactive Spreadsheet: Alongside each post, I’ll link a detailed spreadsheet that tracks breadth and momentum metrics. This will allow you to follow along with the data and see the trends I’m analyzing day-by-day.

  • Quick Video Commentary: To complement the metrics, I’ll also be posting a quick video commentary several days a week. This will provide a more dynamic overview of the market, offering you additional context and clarity.

Market Metrics

Market Backdrop: Mixed

The major indices continue to trend constructively. Large-cap indices are extending higher after finding support at their 10- and 20-day moving averages, while mid- and small-cap indices have resolved upward from recent consolidation ranges. All four indices remain firmly above rising 10-, 20-, and 50-day moving averages, reinforcing positive short- and intermediate-term trend conditions. Price and volume behavior remain orderly, with no evidence of heavy or clustered distribution that would threaten the advance.

Market internals remain supportive but subdued. New highs are still exceeding new lows across the broader market, though the margin remains narrow, signaling selective participation rather than broad-based momentum. A key constraint continues to be the lack of high-quality setups—relatively few stocks are compressing or building tight bases near key moving averages. This suggests that many stocks are either extended from recent moves or still digesting prior volatility, which naturally limits opportunity even within a favorable index-level trend.

Sector leadership continues to rotate. Materials and Financial Services remain at the top of the relative strength rankings. Healthcare has slipped modestly from its prior leadership position, not due to structural damage, but because other sectors have begun to outperform on a relative basis. Industrials, Technology, and Consumer stocks continue to behave constructively from a trend perspective but remain secondary in relative performance. Defensives, Energy, Real Estate, and Utilities persist as laggards, showing both relative and technical weakness.

In summary, the environment remains constructive but selective. The prevailing trend supports long-side exposure, yet narrow participation and a shortage of clean setups argue for patience and disciplined execution rather than aggressive positioning.

Overall Trend: Positive

  • Large Cap: Positive

  • Mid Cap: Positive

  • Small Cap: Positive

Overall NH/NL Breadth: Mixed

  • Large Cap: Positive

  • Mid Cap: Mixed

  • Small Cap: Negative

Overall Up/Down Momentum: Mixed

  • Large Cap: Positive

  • Mid Cap: Mixed

  • Small Cap: Negative

Market Recap

Market Monitor (Click Here)

1. Trend & Market Structure

The primary trend remains intact and constructive.

  • All four major indices are holding above rising 10-, 20-, and 50-day moving averages.

  • Large caps continue to advance after defending short-term support.

  • Mid and small caps have resolved higher from near-term consolidation ranges.

Tactical Guidance

  • Maintain a moderate long bias, but avoid pressing exposure.

  • Allow existing winners to work as long as indices remain above the 20-day MA.

  • Be alert for any loss of the 20-day MA on volume, which would warrant tighter risk controls.

  • No need to get aggressive until price expands decisively beyond recent highs.

2. Breadth & Momentum Monitoring

Internals remain constructive, but confirmation is still lacking.

  • New highs continue to exceed new lows, though only marginally.

  • Breadth and momentum have not expanded meaningfully.

  • Participation remains narrow, limiting follow-through potential.

Tactical Guidance

  • Treat internals as supportive but fragile.

  • Look for confirmation via:

    • Expansion in new highs

    • Broadening upside momentum

  • Until then, expect selective leadership and uneven progress.

3. Sector Allocation & Focus

Leadership remains rotational and concentrated.

Primary Focus

  • Materials

  • Financial Services

  • Healthcare

Secondary / Constructive

  • Industrials

  • Technology

  • Consumer

These groups are acting well technically but lag on a relative basis.

Avoid / Underweight

  • Defensives

  • Energy

  • Real Estate

  • Utilities

Tactical Guidance

  • Concentrate exposure in the top relative strength sectors.

  • Avoid allocating capital to lagging or structurally weak groups.

  • Let relative strength, not anticipation, guide rotation decisions.

4. Stock Selection & Trade Execution

Opportunity remains limited by the lack of clean setups.

Preferred Setups

  • Tight consolidations near rising 10- or 20-day MAs

  • Short-term range breakouts with volume confirmation

  • Relative strength leaders holding structure

Avoid

  • Extended stocks far from support

  • Chasing strength

  • Forcing trades in weak or rotational sectors

Execution Rules

  • Use ½ to ¾ normal position size for new entries.

  • Require clean structure and defined risk.

  • If setups are scarce, staying sidelined is a valid decision.

5. Risk & Position Management

Risk discipline remains key in a selective market.

  • Exposure: Moderate (55–65%)

  • Cash: Maintain 20–30% flexibility

  • Stops: Below recent swing lows or the 20-day MA

  • Trim or exit positions that stall or lose structure.

6. Scenario Planning

Broadening Participation

  • Breadth expands

  • More stocks form tight bases

  • Momentum accelerates

→ Gradually increase exposure toward 70–75%.

Continued Selective Grind

  • Indices trend higher

  • Internals remain narrow

→ Maintain current exposure and focus on best-in-class setups only.

Deterioration

  • Breadth contracts

  • Indices lose the 20-day MA

→ Reduce exposure toward 40–50% and tighten stops.

Bottom Line

The market remains in a constructive uptrend, but opportunity is selective rather than abundant. With breadth only marginally positive and few high-quality setups emerging, patience and precision remain the edge. Let participation broaden before pressing risk; until then, stay focused on leaders, manage exposure carefully, and wait for cleaner opportunities to present themselves.
